Chapter 6. War Arrives: Fear, Loss, and the Unraveling of Home.
There’s a point when distant thunder turns into a full-blown storm right above your head. For families who once hoped the worst would just pass them by, the arrival of war feels like their world’s been turned upside down. Suddenly, the city’s familiar routines vanish—replaced by sirens, blackouts, and a constant, gnawing worry about what tomorrow might bring.
At first, there’s a sense of disbelief. Picture a child, listening as her parents try to explain the unthinkable: bombs falling on neighborhoods, friends' homes destroyed, loved ones missing. The family huddles together in the darkness, counting the seconds between each explosion, quietly hoping their building will be spared. And every morning, they check in with neighbors, feeling grateful for every face that reappears.
War changes everything. School days are cut short by air raids. The playground? Now it’s the basement, where kids whisper stories to each other, trying to block out the noise from above. The child’s father, who once seemed so certain and strong, now carries the weight of worry in his eyes. Her mother’s hands tremble as she prepares meals, carefully rationing food and water, doing her best to keep things feeling normal.
Loss becomes a constant companion. Friends move away, searching for safety in far-off cities or even other countries. Some never come back. The child starts to recognize that certain look in her parents’ eyes—the one that means bad news has arrived. Maybe a neighbor’s son was killed at the front, or a cousin’s home was destroyed. Grief settles over the family like a heavy blanket, but there’s no real time for mourning. Surviving demands their full attention.
And yet, even in the chaos, small acts of kindness still shine through. Neighbors share whatever little they have. Families come together to comfort one another. The child finds comfort in daily rituals—tea with her grandmother, a favorite book read by candlelight, or just the gentle reassurance of her parents’ embrace. These little moments become lifelines. They’re reminders that love can endure, even as the world seems to fall apart.
As the war drags on, the child feels her sense of home slowly unravel. The city she knew is now scarred by violence, and the future looks uncertain. But in all this hardship, she finds a new kind of strength—resilience, born out of adversity, and a stubborn determination to hold on to hope. War may have taken so much, but it can’t destroy the bonds of family, or the will to survive.
